eras.title: Age of the Patriarchs
eras.subtitle: Abraham, Isaac and Jacob
eras.blurb: Abraham leaves Ur for Canaan. The land is a scatter of city-states between the great powers of Egypt and Mesopotamia.

eras.title: Exodus and Wilderness
eras.subtitle: Egypt to Sinai
eras.blurb: Israel leaves Egypt and spends a generation in the wilderness south and east of Canaan.

eras.title: Conquest and Judges
eras.subtitle: Settling the land
eras.blurb: Israel settles among Canaanites, Philistines and the peoples east of the Jordan. No central authority; leadership rises and falls locally.

eras.title: The United Kingdom
eras.subtitle: Saul, David and Solomon
eras.blurb: A single kingdom under three kings, reaching its widest influence under David and Solomon.

eras.title: The Divided Kingdom
eras.subtitle: Israel and Judah
eras.blurb: The kingdom splits after Solomon. Israel in the north and Judah in the south run as rival states for two centuries.

eras.title: Assyrian Ascendancy
eras.subtitle: The fall of the northern kingdom
eras.blurb: Assyria dominates the Near East and destroys Samaria in 722 BC. Judah survives as a tributary.

eras.title: Babylon and the Exile
eras.subtitle: Jerusalem falls
eras.blurb: Babylon replaces Assyria, destroys Jerusalem in 586 BC and carries Judah into exile.

eras.title: The Persian Empire
eras.subtitle: Return from exile
eras.blurb: Cyrus takes Babylon and lets the exiles return. Judah becomes a small province in the largest empire the world had yet seen.

eras.title: Alexander's Empire
eras.subtitle: The Greek conquest
eras.blurb: Alexander takes the whole Persian world in a decade, spreading Greek language and culture across it.

eras.title: The Hasmonean Kingdom
eras.subtitle: Jewish independence
eras.blurb: The Maccabean revolt wins a century of Jewish self-rule before Rome arrives.

eras.title: Rome Arrives
eras.subtitle: The late Republic
eras.blurb: Pompey takes Jerusalem in 63 BC. The eastern Mediterranean passes to Rome.

eras.title: Herod's Kingdom
eras.subtitle: The birth of Jesus
eras.blurb: Herod the Great rules Judea as a client king of Rome. Jesus is born near the end of his reign.

eras.title: The Apostolic Age
eras.subtitle: The church spreads
eras.blurb: The gospel moves out from Jerusalem through the provinces of the empire, along Roman roads and shipping lanes.

eras.title: Rome at its Height
eras.subtitle: The empire at full extent
eras.blurb: Under Trajan the empire reaches its greatest extent, from Britain to the Persian Gulf.

eras.title: The Provinces of Rome
eras.subtitle: The empire organised
eras.blurb: The mature provincial system that the early church grew up inside.

eras.title: The Later Empire
eras.subtitle: Diocletian's reorganisation
eras.blurb: The empire is redivided into many smaller provinces, the shape it carried into the Christian centuries.
